content.overview: Hindu adoption and maintenance are governed primarily by the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Core modules: requisites of valid adoption (s. 6); effects of adoption (s. 12); maintenance of wife (s. 18); widowed daughter-in-law (s. 19); children and aged parents (s. 20).
content.glance: Route: validity of adoption → s. 6; effects → s. 12; wife → s. 18; widowed DIL → s. 19; children/parents → s. 20.
content.study:
Use this overview to route fact patterns to section-specific topics.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Valid adoption — s. 6
sections.body: Capacity to take, give, and be taken; other Chapter conditions (ss. 7–11).

sections.heading: Effects — s. 12
sections.body: Deemed child of adoptive parents; severance of birth ties; three provisos.

sections.heading: Wife — s. 18
sections.body: Maintenance by husband; separate residence grounds; forfeiture for unchastity/conversion.

sections.heading: Widowed daughter-in-law — s. 19
sections.body: Residual claim against father-in-law; inability and remarriage limits.

sections.heading: Children and parents — s. 20
sections.body: Minor children (legitimate/illegitimate); aged/infirm parents unable to maintain themselves.

examples.title: Routing
examples.body: Dispute on whether adoption is valid — open s. 6; claim by aged parent — open s. 20.

hypotheticals.question: Where do you start an HAMA problem?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify whether the issue is adoption validity/effects or a maintenance claimant category, then open the matching section.

misconceptions.trap: HAMA maintenance replaces HMA and CrPC remedies.
misconceptions.correction: Remedies may run in parallel; courts avoid double recovery.
